principles: Single source of truth: registry holds the phase/command/artifact facts; command-policy / DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS / process-fact lifecycle become consumers or are contract-checked against it
Additive and non-behavioral: this story adds projections and a contract test only — zero change to runtime behavior or derived values
Mechanical proof over convention: divergence between the registry and the three existing truth sources must fail a test, not rely on reviewer vigilance
drivers: Three independent truth sources (command-policy allowedPhases, DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS, process-fact lifecycle) can silently drift from the registry
Story 2/3/4 (DONE oracle extraction, orchestrator split, TEST semantics) need a trustworthy registry as their foundation
The B-8db9 combination-bypass class of bug is exactly what an unverified multi-source lifecycle invites

options.name: A: Add commands+artifacts dimensions to registry as projections + a consistency contract test, keep existing sources as-is
pros: Smallest blast radius — no consumer rewrite, command-policy/DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS keep working unchanged
Contract test catches drift mechanically without forcing a risky migration now
Foundation ready for Story 2/3/4 to consume
Zero public behavior change — purely additive
cons: command-policy and DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS remain physically separate files — registry is authoritative-by-contract not authoritative-by-derivation until a later story

options.name: B: Make command-policy and DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS derive FROM the registry now
pros: True single derivation — no possibility of drift
cons: Large rewrite of command-policy.ts (85 entries) and config.ts in one story — high blast radius
Risk of changing public behavior (command legality) — violates the no-behavior-change constraint
Couples the foundation story to a risky migration better done incrementally

options.name: C: Only add a contract test, do not extend the registry
cons: The registry still lacks command/artifact dimensions — the contract test would have nothing canonical to check against
Story 2/3/4 still have no registry command/artifact facts to consume — foundation incomplete

chosen: A: Add commands+artifacts dimensions to registry as projections + a consistency contract test, keep existing sources as-is
rationale: Choose A because it makes the registry the authoritative source-of-truth via a mechanical contract while keeping blast radius minimal — command-policy.ts and DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS keep working byte-identically, and the contract test fails loudly on any drift. Reject B because rewriting 85 command-policy entries plus config.ts to derive from the registry is a high-risk migration that risks changing command legality (public behavior) — that belongs in a later dedicated story, not the foundation step. Reject C because without the registry actually carrying the command/artifact dimensions there is nothing canonical for the contract test to validate against, and Story 2/3/4 would still lack registry facts to consume.

preMortem.scenario: The registry command dimension and DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS legitimately differ (e.g. the * wildcard bucket) and the contract test produces false-positive failures
preMortem.trigger: The contract test does an exact set-equality check without modeling the wildcard/global-command semantics
preMortem.consequence: Every build fails on a non-bug; maintainers disable or ignore the contract test
preMortem.mitigation: The contract test must model the same resolution semantics DEFAULT_PHASE_TOOLS uses (wildcard * bucket + per-phase additions). Test the resolved effective command set per phase, not the raw literal table. Smoke includes a case proving the * bucket commands are accepted in every phase.

preMortem.scenario: Extending the registry changes a value derived by phase-flow.ts or context.ts, silently altering public behavior
preMortem.trigger: A new registry field is accidentally consumed by an existing projection helper
preMortem.consequence: phase ordinals or allowed-transition output changes — a no-behavior-change story breaks behavior
preMortem.mitigation: New dimensions are added as separate exported projections (e.g. lifecycleCommandsByPhase) not woven into existing transition objects consumed by phase-flow. Regression test snapshots phase-flow.ts getPhaseInfo / checkPhaseTransition output for all phases before and after, asserting byte-identical.

preMortem.scenario: The artifacts dimension is modeled too vaguely to be checkable, so it becomes decorative
preMortem.trigger: artifacts is a free-text list with no link to the actual artifact files or the gates that consume them
preMortem.consequence: The artifacts dimension adds noise but no mechanical value; future stories cannot rely on it
preMortem.mitigation: Model artifacts as a typed enum of known artifact files (init-check.json / scope-check.json / delivery-check.json / test-evidence.json / summary.json / declared-artifacts.json / review-passes.json etc.) keyed to the phase/transition that writes them, and have the contract test assert every oracleRows/gate reference that names an artifact resolves to a declared artifact entry.
